name: Autodesk Revit
tagline: Building information modeling software for architecture, structure and MEP, where the 3D model drives the drawing set.

pricing.basis: annual or monthly subscription per user
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Revit is not a drawing app, it is a database of building elements that every downstream deliverable is derived from: plans, sections, schedules, clash coordination, structural and MEP models. An agent can absolutely build you a parametric 3D sketcher that places walls, floors and openings and spits out a plan view, and that is genuinely fun. What it cannot build in a session is the family library, the IFC and RVT round-tripping your engineers expect, the view templates and annotation rules that make a drawing set legible, or the constructability logic baked in over two decades. The deeper problem is social: you do not choose a BIM tool, your project team and the authority reviewing your submission do. A free trial gets you the binary, not the source code, and not the consultants.
coreLoopDIY: A local parametric building modeler: draw walls on a grid, cut door and window openings, stack levels, and auto generate a flat 2D plan plus a door and window schedule, with IFC export.
requirements: An IFC export library if you want anything else to read your model
whatYouLose: Families: thousands of manufacturer-accurate, parametric components you would otherwise model by hand
Coordinated documentation, where changing a wall updates every plan, section, elevation and schedule that references it
Interoperability with structural and MEP consultants who send you RVT and IFC and expect it back
Clash detection, phasing, worksharing and anything resembling multi-discipline collaboration
Deliverables that a plan reviewer, contractor or client will accept without argument
moatNotes: The format is the lock-in. RVT is the de facto exchange currency on large projects, and your file is only as useful as the number of people who can open it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the seat cost is a rounding error against the cost of being the one firm on a project that cannot hand over a model. Revit pricing is brutal and everyone in the industry complains about it loudly and constantly, and then renews, because the alternative is re-drafting coordination by hand and absorbing the liability when something does not fit on site. The software is also deeply embedded in staff skills, office templates, and standard detail libraries that took years to build. A personal replacement solves hobby modeling, not professional delivery.
notes: A parametric wall-and-opening modeler is a genuinely satisfying weekend build. The moat is that the model has to leave your machine: RVT and IFC round-trips with structural, MEP and the plan reviewer are the actual product.
prompt:
Build a local-first parametric building modeler called "tinybim". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + TypeScript, vanilla, no React
- Three.js for the 3D viewport
- Zustand-free: one plain TS store module with subscribe callbacks
- Persistence: the model serializes to a single JSON file, saved to and loaded from disk via the File System Access API, with localStorage autosave as a fallback

Data model, build this first and keep it strict:
- Project has Levels (name, elevation, height)
- WallTypes (name, thickness, layers as name + thickness)
- Walls: level id, start point, end point, type id, height override optional
- Openings: host wall id, distance along wall, width, height, sill height, kind of "door" or "window"
- Slabs: level id, polygon of points, thickness
- Everything has a stable uuid. All edits go through typed store actions. No geometry stored, only parameters.

Features, in scope:
1. Plan editor: top-down 2D canvas with a snapping grid, click-drag to draw walls, snap wall ends to existing wall ends and to the grid. Select and delete.
2. Walls auto-join at shared endpoints: miter the thickness so corners do not overlap visibly.
3. Click a wall to place a door or window at the clicked offset; dimensions editable in a side panel.
4. 3D view: extrude walls with boolean-free opening gaps (split each wall into solid segments around openings), extrude slabs, render levels stacked by elevation.
5. Level switcher: plan editor edits one active level, 3D shows all.
6. Auto-generated schedule table: count of doors and windows grouped by width x height, plus total wall length per wall type. Export schedule as CSV.
7. Export the 3D model as glTF. Add a stub IFC exporter module with a clear TODO comment; do not fake IFC output.

Out of scope, do not build: sections, elevations, annotation, dimensioning, families library, MEP, structural analysis, multi-user editing, any server.

Deliverables: npm install && npm run dev works from an empty folder. README explains the data model and lists exactly what is missing versus real BIM. Include three seeded sample walls so the app is not empty on first load. No .env needed since there are no secrets.
